name: Toy Blocks
description: You are asked to watch your nephew who likes to play with toy blocks in a strange way. He has $$$n$$$ boxes and the $$$i$$$-th box has $$$a_i$$$ blocks. His game consists of two steps: he chooses an arbitrary box $$$i$$$; he tries to move all blocks from the $$$i$$$-th box to other boxes. If he can make the same number of blocks in each of $$$n - 1$$$ other boxes then he will be happy, otherwise, will be sad. Note that your nephew can only move the blocks from the chosen box to the other boxes; he cannot move blocks from the other boxes. You don't want to make your nephew sad, so you decided to put several extra blocks into some boxes in such a way that no matter which box $$$i$$$ he chooses he won't be sad. What is the minimum number of extra blocks you need to put?
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains the integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of boxes. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the number of blocks in each box. It's guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over test cases doesn't exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print a single integer — the minimum number of blocks you need to put. It can be proved that the answer always exists, i. e. the number of blocks is finite.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1452B — Toy Blocks [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
